annotations.text:
Neta desktop canvas, four directions.

Same NoScrubs data in every frame: 14 open missions, 117 agents, the workspace leader Halden selected with Lead++ active for 14 minutes. The navigator, toolbar and chat are identical across all four, so only the canvas mechanism differs.

Each direction answers the open question the manifesto left unresolved: how chronology should be felt, and how tens of missions stay visible and clickable at once. Every frame is at 100% zoom on a 1600 by 1000 window, so the density you see is the density you would get.

Spine. Leading candidate.

Time is a horizontal axis. The leader is now, at the right; missions branch off the spine at their start time, newest nearest the leader, on a log scale so the last hours get the room. Chronology is spatial, not a legend.

Tradeoff: fourteen missions on one axis leave no room. Most missions here show only their live agents plus a chip, short of the eight completed the manifesto asks for, and cards drift up to 290px from their anchors, so the anchor dots and drop edges carry the chronology rather than the cards. Rows are 220px wide here, so about half the task names truncate. Vertical panning is constant when a mission has many agents.

Depth.

Newest work sits in the foreground at full size and contrast; older work recedes, smaller and dimmer, still present and still clickable. Blocked, failed and merged-but-unclosed missions in the back are pulled one tier forward, so attention overrides age.

Tradeoff: at this density the foreground has to occlude the background, so scale and opacity end up carrying recency more than distance does, and most missions show only one or two completed agents before the chip. Freeform placement also needs a stable layout so nodes do not jump between sessions.

Bands.

Vertical time bands read right to left from the leader into the past: Last hour, Today, Yesterday, This week, Earlier. Older bands compress. The calm, practical option and the closest to a native working surface someone could use all day.

Tradeoff: band width caps row width, so task names truncate to a few words, and the two oldest bands sit under the navigator at this window size. The most list-like of the four.

Type.

No card shapes at all. Missions and agents are typeset directly on the ground; ordinal scale and position carry recency, and a hairline ruler along the bottom keeps the timeline honest. The most distinctive of the four.

Tradeoff: text needs more vertical room than cards, so this frame folds every completed agent into the chip, which the manifesto does not allow (up to eight should show). Showing them would roughly double each mission's height. Hit targets and selection states also need care in SwiftUI.

Node system shared by all four directions.

Leader, mission lead, agent in card and row form, the +N completed expander, edge styles, sigils derived from the agent name, and the state and access legend. Agents are identified by name, task, model and access only. No roles.
